ai.title: Fix process-stream regex state
ai.summary: Removed global flag from openTagRegex and closeTagRegex in backend/src/process-stream.ts. Switched from regex.exec to string.match to prevent lastIndex state corruption during tag parsing. Added guard for undefined match.index. Internal refactor, no user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: The tool that reads through your chat messages and picks out special formatting tags (like highlights or notes) now does its matching more carefully, so tags no longer get confused when they appear back-to-back in the stream. It affects anyone relying on structured tags flowing through real-time processing, and you'd notice tags parse consistently instead of occasionally being missed or overlapped. This is a behind-the-scenes fix to how the tag-matching helper behaves internally, with no new features added.

ai.title: Flip DOTENVPATH ternary for RENDER check
ai.summary: Inverted the ternary logic for `DOTENV_PATH` in `backend/src/env.mjs` and `web/src/env.mjs`. When `process.env.RENDER === 'true'`, the path now resolves to `/etc/secrets` instead of `..`. This ensures secrets are loaded from the correct absolute path on Render deployments.

eli5.text: When the software runs on the hosting service called Render, it now looks for secret settings in the system's protected folder instead of trying to go up one level in the file system. The previous version did this backwards, so on Render deployments, the secret settings weren't being found correctly. This affects the parts of the app that run on the server (backend) and the web interface, and it is live today for anyone deploying to Render.

ai.title: Fix DOTENVPATH logic in common/src/db/env.mjs
ai.summary: Inverted ternary operator logic in common/src/db/env.mjs corrected to ensure DOTENV_PATH resolves to '/etc/secrets' when RENDER environment variable is true, defaulting to '..' otherwise. This fixes path resolution for environment configuration files on Render deployments. Change scoped to core database environment loading.

eli5.text: When the app runs on Render hosting, it was picking the wrong spot to look for its environment settings file, which could cause it to fail to load the right configuration. The decision logic for choosing that path was flipped, so apps on Render now correctly read their secrets from '/etc/secrets' instead of looking one folder up. If you deploy on Render, your app should now start up and load configuration properly without manual path fixes.

ai.title: debugLog adds DEBUG prefix to console output
ai.summary: backend/src/util/debug.ts debugLog now calls console.log('[DEBUG]', ...args) before writing to debug.log. File logging behavior unchanged: ISO timestamp prefix, JSON.stringify for objects, appendFileSync. No user-facing change; internal debug tooling only.

eli5.text: When the system runs in debug mode and prints a diagnostic message, it now also shows that message on the screen right away (prefixed with [DEBUG]) in addition to saving it to the debug log file. The log file still works the same way, with timestamps and formatted objects, so nothing about the stored logs changes. This is purely for developers watching the system run; regular users won't see anything different.

ai.title: Update menu tips and feedback email
ai.summary: Updated CLI menu tips in `npm-app/src/menu.ts` to include new usage patterns like refactoring and test fixing. Reordered help commands for better visibility. Changed feedback email address to `james@manicode.ai`.

eli5.text: When you open the interactive menu in the assistant, you'll now see a short list of practical things you can ask it to do, like 'fix my test failures,' 'refactor this big file,' or 'answer my questions about the code.' A few of the older, more generic tips were moved or replaced so these common tasks show up first. The email address you're told to use for feedback has also changed to a new address. These changes are live today and only affect what you see in the in-app help menu.

ai.title: Add start-dir script and refine CLI welcome message
ai.summary: Added `start-dir` npm script in `npm-app/package.json` to run `ts-node src/index.ts` with environment variables. Updated `printInitialPrompt` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to conditionally display a personalized welcome message with an emoji and prompt, or a generic prompt if no user is detected. This improves local development startup options and refines the CLI's initial interaction flow.

eli5.text: When you start the program locally, it now checks if you have a saved profile. If you do, the first screen greets you with a friendly wave emoji and says 'Welcome back [your name]! What would you like to do?'. If no profile is found, it simply shows 'What would you like to do?' without the greeting. Additionally, a new way to launch the program in a specific folder was added, which sets up the right environment settings automatically before starting.

ai.title: Fix applyPatch context match and backslash filter
ai.summary: applyPatch in common/src/util/patch.ts now filters lines starting with backslash and uses inclusive loop bounds in findContextMatch and findContextMatchTrimmed. This prevents patch application failures when context lines appear at the end of files or contain backslash escapes. Tests added in test/__src__/patch.test.ts with mock data in test/__mock-data__/inbox-screen/.

eli5.text: When the system tries to apply a text update to the end of a file, it used to miss changes sitting right at the very bottom or get confused by lines starting with a backslash. Now it properly handles both cases, so the update reaches every line reliably. If you maintain or upgrade a project by pasting an update file (a patch), it now succeeds on files that previously failed at the last line.

ai.title: Fix tool call parsing and stream termination
ai.summary: Corrected tool call parsing in `main-prompt.ts` by wrapping content in `<tool_call>` tags and deferring `isComplete` flag assignment. Updated `process-stream.ts` to return an object with `isComplete` status, allowing the stream generator to terminate early upon detecting a complete tag. Adjusted `tool-handlers.ts` console output for terminal commands to include a newline.

eli5.text: The assistant now correctly recognizes when it receives a complete tool command from the model and stops processing early, instead of treating the command as incomplete text that needs to be echoed back. This fixes a bug where tool calls, like file edits or terminal commands, could be parsed incorrectly, preventing them from executing properly. If you watched the system run, you would see commands now finish cleanly with a line break in the terminal output, and the assistant no longer gets confused when it receives its own tool instructions. The fix is live today for anyone using the assistant through the backend or npm app, so tool-driven actions like editing files or running commands should now work reliably without extra steps.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.72
ai.summary: Incremented version in npm-app/package.json from 1.0.71 to 1.0.72. Added trailing newline to file.

eli5.text: You got a fresh install of the assistant with a couple of fixes that make it run more reliably. Behind the scenes, the team patched a bug that could make text matching go wrong when the assistant reads your files, and they also cleaned up how the assistant decides which settings file to load on your computer. On top of that, some menu tips and the welcome message were updated so the wording feels more helpful when you start it up.

ai.title: Add npm view fallback for manicode version check
ai.summary: The `getManicodeNpmVersion` function in `npm-app/src/update-manicode.ts` now attempts to fetch the latest version via `npm view manicode version` before falling back to web scraping. This change improves reliability by using the native npm CLI, which is faster and less prone to scraping failures than parsing the npmjs.com HTML. The implementation includes a regex match for semantic versioning and silently catches errors to trigger the existing `scrapeWebPage` fallback if the command fails.

eli5.text: When you ask the app to check for a new version of Manicode, it now first tries the built-in npm tool to find the latest version number, which is faster and more reliable than the old method of downloading the npm website and reading the version out of the page. If that npm tool call fails for any reason, the app quietly falls back to the old website-reading method, so version checking never completely breaks. The change only affects the internal version-check step, so you wouldn't see a new visible feature, but the check itself is now less likely to fail due to website scraping problems.

ai.title: Refactor stream handling in backend/src/main-prompt.ts
ai.summary: Refactors streaming logic in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to separate raw accumulation from display processing. Introduces `printedChunk` to handle `<file>` tag stripping and formatting before user display, while `fullResponse` retains raw content. Updates `onTagStart` and `onTagEnd` handlers to emit and close `<file>` tags correctly. This internal change ensures file editing status messages display cleanly without leaking raw XML tags to the UI.

eli5.text: When the assistant tells you it is editing a file, the message shown to you is now cleaner and no longer contains raw formatting tags that were accidentally leaking through to the display. This is an internal adjustment to how streaming text is processed, so nothing about what the assistant does has changed, just how the in-progress status messages look while it works.

ai.title: Version 1.0.73
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.73. Update recorded in `npm-app/package.json`. Internal maintenance.

eli5.text: If you downloaded or updated the AI dev assistant today, you're now on the latest release, which packages together a few small behind-the-scenes improvements that make it more reliable. This release adds a fallback check when the assistant looks up its own version information online, and smooths out how responses are streamed back to you as the assistant types. You won't see new buttons or menus, but the assistant may connect a little more smoothly when something it needs isn't immediately available. These changes take effect for anyone running the latest version.

ai.title: Refine knowledge generation prompt and tests
ai.summary: Adjusted knowledge generation prompt in backend/src/generate-knowledge-files.ts to prioritize user expectation mismatches over code clarity, and added instructions for preserving existing file content during updates. Updated test mock data in test/__mock-data__/knowledge-files to reflect new tool call formats and expected file changes. Renamed test script in test/package.json from test-generate-knowledge to test-knowledge.

eli5.text: The instructions guiding how new knowledge files are created were tweaked so the system now prioritizes whether an assistant's response failed to meet what you actually expected, rather than focusing on how clear the code looked to another developer. A few internal testing files were also updated to match this new approach, and one test command was renamed from 'test-generate-knowledge' to 'test-knowledge' for simplicity. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping that doesn't change what you see, but keeps the system's self-improvement process more aligned with your expectations.

ai.title: Add env var validation to npm-app build
ai.summary: Added missing environment variable checks in `npm-app/loadEnv.js` before build completion. Validation ensures `APP_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL` are present and non-empty. Scope limited to npm-app build tooling.

eli5.text: When you build the internal npm app, it now checks that two key settings (the app's web address and the backend server address) are properly configured before finishing. If either is missing or empty, the build stops and alerts you to add them. This affects only the npm-app build tooling and prevents incomplete builds from proceeding.

ai.title: Inject recently read files into system prompt
ai.summary: System prompt now includes top 20 recently read file paths based on OS atime. FileTreeNode schema extended with filePath and lastReadTime. getProjectFileTree in common/src/project-file-tree.ts captures atimeMs during traversal. Backend system-prompt.ts renders these paths in a new <recently_read_file_paths_most_recent_first> block to provide context.

eli5.text: The assistant now gets a short memory boost: alongside the project files you've opened, the system prompt now lists the 20 most recently viewed file paths, surfaced as a readable block so the assistant can pick up where you left off in a conversation. This list is assembled during a normal project scan that now records when each file was last opened, so it appears automatically when a project context is built. It is live today whenever you start a new conversation against a project, as the prompt that guides the assistant already includes the new recently-read paths alongside its other hints about your files.

ai.title: updateManicode skips local dev
ai.summary: updateManicode now early-returns when `isProduction` is false. Prevents npm version checks and updates in local dev. Internal change in `npm-app/src/update-manicode.ts`.

eli5.text: When you run the software on your own computer for testing, it now skips checking for and installing updates entirely. This means local development sessions won't contact the update server or try to change the installed version while you're working. The change affects only local setups; production deployments still check for updates as before. If you looked at the code, you'd see a simple early exit that prevents the update process from starting outside of a production environment.

ai.title: Ignore minified files in project file tree
ai.summary: Adds `*.min.*` to default ignore list in `getProjectFileTree` within `common/src/project-file-tree.ts`. Reduces noise by excluding minified assets from file tree traversal and indexing. Refactors `getLastReadFilePaths` signature for multi-line parameter formatting.

eli5.text: The assistant now hides minified files from your project file list, so you'll see fewer irrelevant build artifacts cluttering your view. When browsing a project, files matching patterns like `*.min.js` are automatically filtered out of the default ignore list. This is a minor housekeeping improvement, so you won't need to wait for an activation date; it just works as soon as the assistant scans a project.
